name: 汐まち寿司 つるみ (Shiomachi Sushi Tsurumi)

claims.text: Sushi service and the sweet anago tare glaze rely on standard soy-sauce-based seasonings, which contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Even the rice is cooked in a kombu-and-bonito dashi and bonito flakes are used within dishes, so fish products are pervasive throughout the kitchen.

name: 汁なし担担麺 味源 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Ajigen)

claims.text: The dish is a brothless dan dan noodle made with wheat noodles and a soy/sesame seasoning, which conventionally contains wheat-based soy sauce.

name: 汁なし担担麺 きさく (Shirunashi Tantanmen Kisaku)

claims.text: The kitchen is a single-dish wheat-noodle counter; noodles are boiled in shared water and the sauce contains gluten-bearing seasonings, so gluten contact is unavoidable.
The signature sauce is a chicken-and-dried-sardine broth blend; no gluten-free soy sauce is indicated and standard wheat-based seasoning should be assumed.
The core dish uses ground meat and a fish/chicken broth sauce, and is prepared on a single shared counter line, so animal ingredients are integral to the only menu item.

name: 汁なし担々麺 麻沙羅 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Masara)

claims.text: Sichuan-style soupless tantan noodles such as those served here are made with wheat noodles and seasoned with chili/sesame sauces that conventionally include wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free option is documented.
The dish is built on minced pork and animal-derived seasoning typical of tantan noodles; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: 汁なし担担麺 武蔵坊 地蔵通り本店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Musashibo (Jizo-dori Ho)

claims.text: Core dish is wheat noodles; soy-sauce version uses standard soy sauce. A shared kitchen handling wheat throughout means high gluten cross-contact risk.
The aromatic soy-sauce (芳醇醤油) bowl is built on soy sauce, which in Japan is typically brewed with wheat.
All bowls contain ground pork as a standard topping; no meat-free preparation is offered.

name: 汁なし担担麺 武蔵坊 じぞう通り本店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Musashibo (Jizo-dori Ma)

claims.text: The dish is built on wheat noodles, so the entire menu centers on gluten; there is no documented gluten-free preparation or separate handling.
The savory sauce for shiru-nashi tantanmen is typically soy-sauce based, which in Japan generally contains wheat; no gluten-free tamari is documented.
Ground pork is mixed directly into the noodles as a core component, so all bowls are prepared with meat and there is no documented vegan separation.

name: 汁なし担担麺専門 キング軒 本通店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Senmon King-ken Hondori)

claims.text: The kitchen is built around wheat noodles and a wheat-based soy tare, so any dish risks gluten contact; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The soy tare is hand-made using a 'King-ken' soy sauce specially commissioned from Kawanaka Shoyu (founded 1906), a conventional wheat-fermented Japanese soy sauce.
The signature dish includes a minced-pork topping and is prepared in a kitchen dedicated to meat-based dandan noodles, so vegan cross-contact is unavoidable.

name: 自然食レストラン かんな (Shizenshoku Restaurant Kanna)

claims.text: As a Japanese natural-food kitchen, miso and soy-sauce-based seasonings used here typically contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Cooking emphasizes pesticide-free and organic vegetables and additive-free, traditionally fermented seasonings, which appeals to clean-eating diners.
